content.value_statement: Stacked pull requests can be hard to manage with plain Git commands. This skill gives direct Graphite CLI workflows for creating, submitting, syncing, and restructuring stacks.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Graphite CLI commands for stacked pull request workflows.
Guides setup with `gt auth` and `gt init` before creating stacks.
Describes how to create, submit, and update Graphite branches and pull requests.
Provides navigation commands for moving through stack branches.
Explains synchronization, conflict resolution, and cleanup after merge.
Covers advanced stack changes such as move, fold, split, insert, and absorb.
limitations: Does not install or configure the Graphite CLI for the user.
Does not verify the current repository state unless the agent runs local commands separately.
Does not replace Graphite official documentation for the newest CLI changes.
Requires user approval before commands modify branches, commits, or remote pull requests.

use_cases.title: Create a First Stack
use_cases.description: Learn how to initialize a repository, create dependent branches, and submit draft pull requests.

use_cases.title: Maintain Review Feedback
use_cases.description: Apply requested changes, amend commits, restack dependent branches, and update pull requests.

use_cases.title: Restructure Complex Work
use_cases.description: Choose Graphite commands for moving, folding, splitting, inserting, or absorbing changes across a stack.

prompt_templates.title: Start With Graphite
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up Graphite CLI in this repository and explain each command before I run it.

prompt_templates.title: Create Stacked PRs
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a feature to split into three pull requests. Plan the Graphite CLI commands for creating and submitting the stack.

prompt_templates.title: Sync and Resolve Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: My Graphite stack is behind trunk and may have conflicts. Guide me through sync, conflict resolution, and resubmission.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure an Existing Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current stack shape and recommend whether to use gt move, gt fold, gt split, gt create --insert, or gt absorb.

output_examples.input: How do I submit all branches in my current Graphite stack?
output_examples.output: Move to the top branch, review the stack with `gt log short`, then use `gt submit --stack`. Submit as draft if the stack is not ready for review.

output_examples.input: I changed code after review on the middle branch of a stack.
output_examples.output: Check out the branch with the review change, amend it with `gt modify -a`, resolve any restack conflicts, then run `gt submit` or `gt submit --stack`.

output_examples.input: When should I use gt absorb?
output_examples.output: Use it when unstaged fixes belong to different downstack commits. Review the proposed changes carefully before updating and resubmitting the stack.

best_practices: Run status and log commands before Graphite operations that change branches or pull requests.
Keep each stack layer small, reviewable, and focused on one logical change.
Submit draft pull requests when a stack needs early review but is not ready to merge.
anti_patterns: Do not run stack-changing commands without confirming the current branch and parent branch.
Do not combine unrelated work into one Graphite branch when separate stack layers are clearer.
Do not force stack cleanup if unresolved review feedback or merge conflicts remain.

faq.question: What is Graphite CLI used for?
faq.answer: It helps developers create, submit, sync, and manage stacked pull requests from the command line.

faq.question: Does this skill run Graphite commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance. Any command execution depends on the host agent and user approval.

faq.question: Can it help with merge conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the normal Graphite flow for resolving conflicts, staging fixes, and continuing the interrupted operation.

faq.question: Can it manage coworker stacks?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference material covers collaboration commands such as fetching, freezing, unfreezing, and tracking branches.

faq.question: Is official Graphite documentation still needed?
faq.answer: Yes. Use official documentation for installation details, authentication changes, and newly released CLI options.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
